content: This medication may, in rare cases, lead to severe and potentially fatal complications due to blood clots, such as heart attacks, strokes, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are uncommon. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco products while on this medication. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning to have surgery, or will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially if you are using an estrogen-containing product. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin or face (melasma). Sunlight can exacerbate this effect, so limit your exposure to the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Some estrogen products contain mineral oil, which can weaken rubber products like latex condoms, cervical caps, and diaphragms, potentially leading to their failure. If you are unsure whether your product contains mineral oil, consult your pharmacist. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce both the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing inaccurate results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, and Pap smears), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can help reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving crossword puzzles) may help prevent dementia. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
